bull_bear.body:
- Long-tenured customer base: more than seventy percent of business comes from customers who have been with the company more than ten years
- Deepened engagements with existing customers, added new capabilities and won multiple strategic accounts in past years
- Breadth of engineering services across Plant Engineering, Architecture and Construction, Aerospace and niche allied industries
- International delivery footprint via three wholly-owned foreign subsidiaries (USA, Switzerland, UK)
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Developed-market demand concentration - North America and Europe — Management explicitly flags that a potential slowdown in the North American or European economies could exert a dampening effect on the Company's overall growth trajectory. TAAL Tech's customers sit in North America, Europe and APAC, so the revenue base is directly exposed to those two economies' capital and engineering-spend cycles.
- Global geopolitical and macroeconomic risk — Stated verbatim: although the macro-outlook for growth in the ER&D space remains positive, 'global geopolitical and economic risks persist'. This is the framing risk management places around an otherwise positive outlook.
- AI disruption of the engineering services model - impact not yet assessable — Management states it is 'yet to be able to assess the full impact of AI on the engineering services sector' and will assess it as it goes along. For a labour-based ER&D services provider this is an unquantified structural risk to the pricing and effort-based revenue model; the stated response is to stay abreast of industry trends and adopt the technology to improve efficiencies.
- Customer concentration / dependence on long-tenured key accounts — A structural concentration disclosure not labelled as a risk: 'more than seventy percent of our business comes from customers who have been with us more than ten years'. Strategy is explicitly to grow 'around key strategic customers'. The relationship depth is presented as a strength, but it also means the majority of revenue rests on a small set of long-standing accounts.
- Talent dependence in a people-based ER&D business — The MD&A states 'Human Resource Management is critical to the successful functioning of our Company' and that it is the Company's endeavour to nurture a high-performance culture focused on efficiency, innovation and talent growth. Capability and headcount are the delivery capacity of an asset-light services firm. Note: no attrition rate, headcount or utilisation figure is disclosed in the routed text.
- Cross-border / foreign-currency and multi-jurisdiction operating exposure — All three subsidiaries are foreign (USA, Switzerland, UK) and revenue is earned from North America, Europe and APAC customers; the Board's Report notes that foreign exchange earnings and outgo particulars are given as Annexure A. The FX and multi-jurisdiction exposure is structural, though the Company does not itself label it a risk in the routed text.
- Execution/integration risk around the merger and the change of corporate identity — TAAL Enterprises Limited merged with its wholly owned subsidiary TAAL Tech India Private Limited during the year and the merged entity was renamed TAAL Tech Limited to retain brand recognition. Management states the merger was 'effected smoothly without any interruption to business', so this is a disclosed-and-mitigated item rather than an open risk, but it changes the reporting entity and the comparability of the corporate history.
- Statutory auditor discontinuity - casual vacancy filled mid-year — M/s. V P Thacker & Co. were re-appointed as Statutory Auditors at the 11th AGM for five years till the 16th AGM, but during the year that firm merged with M/s. Lodha & Bhatt, creating a casual vacancy; the Board appointed M/s. TLB & Co. on February 10, 2026 to hold office until the conclusion of the 12th AGM. Mitigants disclosed: the statutory audit report carries an unmodified opinion with no qualification, reservation, adverse remark or disclaimer; the Secretarial Audit Report likewise carries no qualification; and neither auditor reported any instance of fraud under Section 143(12) during the year.
- Generic forward-looking-statement risk factors — The MD&A cautionary statement names demand-supply conditions, changes in Government regulations, tax regime, economic developments within the country and litigation as factors that could make a difference to the Company's operations. Boilerplate, but it is the only place litigation is mentioned at all.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: TAAL Tech provides ER&D services, with core areas of expertise in Plant Engineering, Architecture and Construction, Aerospace and certain niche allied industries. Within each of these industry verticals it provides a wide range of engineering services including manufacturing engineering and digital support. Its three foreign subsidiaries provide ER&D services customised to the specific needs of every individual customer.

business.title: Products & brands

business.body:
- TAAL Technologies Inc., USA — subsidiary: Wholly-owned foreign subsidiary, 100% shareholding, reporting currency US $; provides ER&D services customised to the specific needs of every individual customer.
- TAAL Tech GmbH, Switzerland — subsidiary: Wholly-owned foreign subsidiary, 100% shareholding, reporting currency CHF; provides ER&D services.
- TAAL Tech (UK) Limited — subsidiary: Wholly-owned foreign subsidiary, 100% shareholding, reporting currency GBP; expressly named in AOC-1 Note A as a subsidiary that is yet to commence operations.
- TAAL Tech India Private Limited — subsidiary: Former wholly owned subsidiary that was amalgamated into the Company under an NCLT-approved scheme during the year; the merged entity was then renamed TAAL Tech Limited (formerly TAAL Enterprises Limited). No longer a separate entity at year-end; it does not appear in the AOC-1 subsidiary roster. Sitting fees for Mr. Muralidhar Chittetti Reddy are annotated in the remuneration table as relating to TAAL Tech India Pvt. Ltd.
- Taneja Aerospace and Aviation Limited — related party: Listed entity on whose board four of TAAL Tech's directors sit: Mr. Salil Taneja as Promoter-NED (common promoter linkage), Mr. Arvind Nanda as Independent Director up to September 30, 2025, and Ms. Deepa Mathur and Mr. Anil Kumar Sahu as Independent Directors w.e.f. 08-08-2025. Disclosed only via the listed-entity directorship table; it is not named as a subsidiary, associate or joint venture, and no transaction with it is disclosed.

business.body:
- Long-tenured customer base: more than seventy percent of business comes from customers who have been with the company more than ten years
- Deepened engagements with existing customers, added new capabilities and won multiple strategic accounts in past years
- Breadth of engineering services across Plant Engineering, Architecture and Construction, Aerospace and niche allied industries

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Be a market leader in its ER&D industry segments and grow capabilities and business around key strategic customers.
- Deepen engagements with existing customers, add new capabilities and win strategic accounts (stated as what has been done in past years and expected to continue yielding).
- Concentrate the group structure for clarity and focus: TAAL Enterprises Limited merged with its wholly owned subsidiary TAAL Tech India Private Limited, with the merged entity renamed TAAL Tech Limited to retain the brand identity built in the marketplace.
- Adopt AI technology to improve efficiencies while assessing its full impact on the engineering services sector.
- Serve customers across North America, Europe and APAC in Plant Engineering, Architecture and Construction, Aerospace and niche allied industries, spanning manufacturing engineering and digital support.
- Nurture a high-performance HR culture focused on efficiency, innovation and talent growth.
- Sustain environmental/sustainability commitment (evidenced by EcoVadis certification) and social responsibility through a CSR Policy.
- The routed governance text states no dividend policy, payout ratio, buyback, debt-reduction or reinvestment philosophy. What it does state on capital/compensation structure: the Company does not have any Employee Stock Option Scheme; a Remuneration Policy framed on the recommendation of the NRC is in place, under which remuneration/sitting fees for the Managing Director, KMP and Senior Management are decided by the Board based on criteria such as industry benchmarks, financial performance of the Company and performance of Directors/KMP; the Company pays remuneration by way of salary, perquisites and allowances to its Managing Director, and no remuneration was paid by way of commission to any Non-Executive Director; during the year sitting fees payable to Non-Executive Directors were revised to Rs. 30,000 each for Board and Audit Committee meetings and Rs. 15,000 each for all other committee meetings. Governance framework: Board of 6 directors as on March 31, 2026 in conformity with Regulation 17 of the Listing Regulations, with 4 Independent Directors including a Woman Director; 5 Board meetings held during FY2025-26 (May 28 2025, August 04 2025, November 11 2025, January 06 2026, February 10 2026); Audit Committee met 4 times; NRC met twice; SRC met once (February 10, 2026); the CSR Committee was constituted on August 04, 2025 and no CSR Committee meeting was required to be held during the year; Independent Directors met separately on March 25, 2026. AOC-2 discloses NA against every particular for both non-arm's-length and material arm's-length related-party contracts, i.e. no such contracts were reported for FY2025-26.
- Environmental/sustainability: the Company states a strong commitment to protecting the environment and to sustainability, 'reflected in our recent Ecovadis certification'. This is the only third-party ESG accreditation disclosed; no rating level, score or award date is given.
- Social/CSR: a robust CSR Policy is in place, 'aimed at creating a positive and lasting impact on society and the communities that we serve'. The Company states it has duly complied with Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013 and that the Annual Report on CSR Activities for FY ended March 31, 2026 forms part of the Board's Report as 'Annexure D' (the annexure itself was not routed, so CSR spend, projects and any unspent amount are not visible here). A CSR Committee exists under Section 135.
- Governance/ethics: a Whistle Blower Policy / Vigil Mechanism established by the Board is available on the Company's website; the Nomination and Remuneration Policy is also published on the website.
- Risk governance: 'The Company has a robust risk management framework to identify and mitigate risks arising out of internal as well as external factors' - a framework assertion only, with no risk register, no Risk Management Committee named and no material-issue table.
- Controls assurance: the Directors' Responsibility Statement confirms internal financial controls were laid down and were adequate and operating effectively, that accounts were prepared on a going-concern basis, and that systems to ensure compliance with all applicable laws were adequate and operating effectively; the MD&A separately asserts a proper and adequate system of internal controls safeguarding assets against loss from unauthorised use or disposition.
- Human capital: stated endeavour to nurture a high-performance culture with a clear focus on efficiency, innovation and talent growth - narrative only, with no headcount, diversity, attrition, safety or training metric disclosed.
- Energy/emissions: no BRSR was routed and no energy, emissions, water or waste data appears; the Board's Report only cross-references Section 134(3)(m) particulars on conservation of energy, technology absorption and foreign exchange earnings and outgo as 'Annexure A', which was not supplied.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The routed text discloses no capex project, plant, capacity addition, new delivery centre, commissioning or ramp-up plan. The only structural/expansion-type event disclosed is corporate rather than physical: during FY2025-26 TAAL Enterprises Limited merged with its wholly owned subsidiary TAAL Tech India Private Limited and the merged entity was renamed TAAL Tech Limited, with the merger effected without interruption to business. On the operating side management describes capability-led rather than asset-led growth - deepening engagements with existing customers, adding new capabilities and winning multiple strategic accounts in past years, and taking steps to adopt AI technology to improve efficiencies. TAAL Tech is an asset-light ER&D services company serving North America, Europe and APAC, and its international footprint consists of three wholly-owned foreign subsidiaries (TAAL Technologies Inc. USA, TAAL Tech GmbH, TAAL Tech UK Ltd.); no rupee capital-expenditure quantum is stated anywhere in this bundle.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- The ER&D sector offers ample growth opportunities driven by the need to bring products to market faster and in a more cost-effective manner, and TAAL Tech is stated to be well positioned to take advantage of this trend.
- The macro-outlook for growth in the ER&D space remains positive, though global geopolitical and economic risks persist.
- A potential slowdown in the North American or European economies could exert a dampening effect on the overall growth trajectory.
- The full impact of AI on the engineering services sector is not yet assessable; management will assess it as it goes along.
- Customer stickiness: more than seventy percent of business comes from customers of more than ten years' standing.
- Outlook stated as 'very positive'; past-year efforts (deeper existing-customer engagements, new capabilities, multiple strategic accounts won) are expected to continue to yield very positive results in the coming years.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers
